title: What is working capital?
subtitle: Working Capital - the daily fuel that runs a business
explanation: Working capital is the gap between current assets and current liabilities - the buffer for day-to-day operations. Positive means a safety margin, but too much positive can be a sign cash is dying in inventory and receivables. Negative isn't automatically bad either: supermarkets and businesses that collect cash upfront often run sustainably negative working capital, because customers pay them before they have to pay their suppliers.

diagram.label: Subtract current liabilities: payables, debt due
Positive means a buffer; negative needs checking that cash inflow is steady enough

realWorldExample.description: PNJ (Phú Nhuận Jewelry) needs large working capital to maintain gold and gem inventory across hundreds of stores - efficient working-capital management is a matter of survival for retailers with high inventory value.

quiz.question: Working Capital (WC) =
options: Current Assets − Current Liabilities
Total Assets − Total Liabilities
Current Assets ÷ Liabilities
Cash + Inventory
quiz.explanation: WC = CA - CL. It measures the ability to pay off current liabilities.

quiz.question: WC = 500 million - is that good?
options: Not certain - it depends on the industry
Not certain - it depends on the company's scale
Good, because a positive WC is always a good sign
Bad, because 500 million is far too low a level
quiz.explanation: WC = 500m against 10,000 billion in revenue = very low. WC = 500m against 100m in revenue = high.

quiz.question: A negative WC:
options: Bad, because the company is losing money for the period
Has no bearing on financial health whatsoever
Always good because the company is using supplier capital
Bad, current liabilities exceed current assets
quiz.explanation: A negative WC = a liquidity crisis. The company owes more than it has on hand.

quiz.question: To improve WC, a company should:
options: Convert long-term debt into current debt, since that raises current assets too
Increase current debt to get more cash right away
Buy more fixed assets using cash
Increase current assets or decrease current liabilities
quiz.explanation: All three approaches would increase WC.

quiz.question: Retail often has negative WC because:
options: It collects cash immediately from sales but pays suppliers slowly
It sells to customers on credit while paying its own suppliers right away in cash
Inventory always makes up a very large proportion
The retail industry's margins are inherently very thin
quiz.explanation: Amazon and Walmart have negative WC yet succeed because their cash cycle is optimised.

quiz.question: A high Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO):
options: Good, it proves strong market demand
Bad, goods sit in the warehouse a long time, cash is tied up
Has no effect at all on working capital
Good, it shows the company always has plenty of stock ready to sell
quiz.explanation: High DIO = goods sit in the warehouse a long time = cash comes in slowly.

quiz.question: To optimise WC with a supplier:
options: Pay suppliers early every time to secure a payment discount
Order more to get a better price
Negotiate a longer payment term (increasing AP)
Switch to buying on immediate cash terms
quiz.explanation: Increasing AP = holding onto cash. But balance the business relationship.

keyTakeaways: Positive WC: a buffer; negative WC: needs careful management
Changes in WC directly affect OCF

practicePrompt.question: A manufacturing company has Current Assets = 400 billion, Current Liabilities = 600 billion. What is this company's Working Capital (WC), and what does it mean?
options: WC = -200 billion: current liabilities exceed current assets, so watch the near-term obligations
WC = 1,000 billion (positive) because you add the two figures together under the total-assets formula
WC = 200 billion (positive) - the company has an adequate financial buffer, no need to worry about liquidity at all
WC cannot be calculated without information about the company's equity
practicePrompt.explanation: WC = Current Assets − Current Liabilities = 400 - 600 = -200 billion (negative). A negative WC means current liabilities exceed current assets - the company needs to manage its cash flow carefully to ensure it can pay obligations as they come due, though a negative WC isn't always a bad sign (some retail business models run well with negative WC).

summary.commonMistake: Reading a concept as a phrase to memorise rather than a principle to apply to real decisions.
summary.action: Positive WC: a buffer; negative WC: needs careful management

application.title: Calculate your own personal working capital
application.message: Take total assets convertible to cash within 12 months (cash, short-term savings) minus total liabilities due over the next 12 months - that's your own personal working capital.
application.secondary: A positive number means you have a buffer; a negative number is a signal to adjust spending or income.

sections.text: Working Capital is the capital a business needs to run day-to-day operations - buying materials, paying salaries, holding inventory - before it collects cash from customers. **Formula:** Working Capital = Current Assets − Current Liabilities.

When current assets exceed current liabilities, a business has a 'buffer' to cover near-term obligations even during a temporary rough patch. This is common in manufacturing businesses - they need substantial capital to buy raw materials, hold inventory, and wait for customers to pay before recovering that capital.
Negative Working Capital - not always bad

Some business models run with negative WC deliberately and healthily. Supermarkets and retail chains collect cash/card payments immediately from customers but pay suppliers 30-60 days later - they operate on supplier money without needing much of their own capital. This is a structural advantage, not a danger sign, as long as operating cash flow stays positive and stable.

items: Large positive WC: safe, but may be holding too much idle capital in inventory/AR
Deliberate negative WC (retail, budget airlines): a structural advantage, collecting cash before paying it out
Unintentional negative WC (a business in real difficulty): genuine liquidity risk

sections.label: PNJ and its gold inventory
sections.text: PNJ needs large working capital to maintain gold and gem inventory across hundreds of stores nationwide - for an industry with high-value inventory like jewellery, efficient working-capital management is a matter of survival that determines the real profit margin.

concepts.def: Current Assets − Current Liabilities, the capital needed to run daily operations
Cash, receivables, inventory - converted to cash within 12 months

lines: Working Capital measures short-term operating health, not profit.
Negative WC isn't automatically bad - it depends on the business model and operating cash flow.
Changes in WC over each period are one of the three main components of operating cash flow (OCF).
